candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: owner
candidates.comment: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.

candidates.label: subOrganization
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a parent organization and a smaller organization that is a part of it, such as a subsidiary. Also called "subsidiary", "division", "affiliated organization", "part of organization". Examples: "Google has subOrganization YouTube", "The university's subOrganization is the Computer Science Department", "This company owns several subOrganization entities.". Distinct from department, which is a more specific type of sub-organization.

candidates.label: parentOrganization
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between an organization and the larger organization it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is a division of, is a subsidiary of, is part of. Examples: Google is a parent organization of YouTube. A local branch is a parent organization of its national headquarters. A department is a parent organization of its university. Distinct from subOrganization, which points from a larger organization to its smaller components.

candidates.label: parent
candidates.comment: A person who is a parent of another person. Also called mother, father, progenitor. Examples: "Child A parent 'Parent B'", "Person X parent 'Mother Y'", "Person Z parent 'Father W'". Distinct from children, which describes the offspring.

candidates.label: branchOf
candidates.comment: An organization that a local business is a branch of. Also called: parent organization, corporate parent, subsidiary of. Examples: "LocalBusiness 'Local Cafe' branchOf 'Coffee Chain Inc.'", "LocalBusiness 'Branch Bank' branchOf 'National Bank'". Distinct from branch, which refers to anatomical nerve branches.

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: parentItem
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a discussion item and its preceding item or a creative work it comments on. Also called part of, replies to, refers to, is a response to. Examples: A comment is a parent item of another comment. A question is a parent item of an answer. An answer is a parent item of a follow-up comment. Distinct from comment, which points from something to a comment about it.

candidates.label: parentService
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a broadcast service and a broader broadcast service it is a variation or component of. Also called belongs to, is a variation of, is part of, is a channel of. Examples: BBC One Scotland is a parent service of BBC One. A regional news channel is a parent service of a national news channel. A specific sports channel is a parent service of a broader sports network.

candidates.label: copyrightHolder
candidates.comment: A legal ownership relation between a creative work and the person or organization holding its copyright. Also called: copyright owner, rights holder, legally owned by. Examples: "The Mona Lisa" copyright holder "The Louvre Museum", "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" copyright holder "J.K. Rowling", "Microsoft Windows" copyright holder "Microsoft Corporation".

Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: significance
candidates.comment: The medical or diagnostic importance of superficial anatomy, indicating how its characteristics may suggest underlying conditions or treatments. Also called clinical relevance, diagnostic implication, anatomical importance. Examples: `Skin Lesion` significance `"May indicate melanoma"`, `Swollen Lymph Node` significance `"Could suggest infection"`, `Discolored Nail Bed` significance `"Possible circulatory issue"`.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: positiveNotes
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute providing positive considerations, highlights, or pros for a product or an item being reviewed. Also called pros, advantages, benefits, highlights. Examples: A product has positive notes like 'Excellent battery life'. A review has positive notes like 'User-friendly interface'. The service has positive notes like 'Responsive customer support'. Distinct from negativeNotes, which provides negative considerations.

candidates.label: partOfEpisode
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a clip and the episode it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is featured in, belongs to, is from. Examples: A highlight reel is part of an episode. A deleted scene is part of an episode. A short preview is part of an episode.

candidates.label: reviewAspect
candidates.comment: The specific part, feature, or facet of an item that a review or rating pertains to. Also called review focus, aspect reviewed, rating dimension. Examples: `Restaurant Review` reviewAspect `"Service Quality"`, `Product Rating` reviewAspect `"Battery Life"`, `Movie Review` reviewAspect `"Acting Performance"`.

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: aspect
candidates.comment: A specific area or topic of medical practice considered on a medical webpage. Also called: medical topic, health aspect, clinical focus. Examples: "MedicalWebPage 'Diabetes' aspect 'diagnosis'", "MedicalWebPage 'Flu' aspect 'treatment'", "MedicalWebPage 'Cancer' aspect 'prognosis'."

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

chosen_property.label: disclosedEvent
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the event that was revealed or made public by the subject.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly captures an organization disclosing an event.

candidates.label: unnamedSourcesPolicy
candidates.comment: An unnamed sources policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a statement about its policy on using unnamed sources. Also called anonymous sources policy, source confidentiality policy, disclosure policy. Examples: "NewsMediaOrganization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/sources-policy'", "Organization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'Our policy requires two independent sources.'", "News outlet unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/ethics'".

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: isAccessibleForFree
candidates.comment: An access cost relation indicating whether a creative work, event, or place can be accessed without charge. Also called free access, no charge, complimentary access, free of cost. Examples: A public park has isAccessibleForFree set to 'true'. An online article has isAccessibleForFree set to 'true'. A concert has isAccessibleForFree set to 'false'.

candidates.label: archiveHeld
candidates.comment: An archive held relation between an archive organization and a collection, fonds, or item maintained by it. Also called archival holding, collection maintained, item preserved. Examples: "The National Archives' archive held is 'Presidential Papers'.", "The historical society's archive held is 'Local Family Records'."

candidates.label: domiciledMortgage
candidates.comment: A domiciled mortgage relation between a mortgage loan and a boolean value indicating whether the borrower is a resident of the jurisdiction where the property is located. Also called "resident borrower", "local mortgage", "in-jurisdiction loan". Examples: "Mortgage loan domiciledMortgage 'true'", "Property loan domiciledMortgage 'false' for foreign resident", "Home mortgage domiciledMortgage 'true'".

candidates.label: companyRegistration
candidates.comment: An official registration relation for an organization, providing its business registration information as a certification. Also called "business registration", "corporate certification", "legal registration". Examples: "Company organization companyRegistration 'Company House Certificate'", "Non-profit organization companyRegistration 'Charity Commission Registration'".

candidates.label: ownershipFundingInfo
candidates.comment: Information describing the ownership structure, funding, and grants of an organization, particularly concerning editorial independence for news media. Also called funding transparency, ownership structure, financial backing details. Examples: "News Org A ownershipFundingInfo 'https://news.example.com/about/funding'", "Company B ownershipFundingInfo 'Privately held by XYZ Group.'", "Nonprofit C ownershipFundingInfo 'Funded by grants from various foundations.'". Distinct from funder, which specifically identifies the entity providing funds.

candidates.label: ownedFrom
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was obtained. Also called acquisition date, purchase date, date acquired. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2020-01-15'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2018-06-01T10:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2023-03-10'". Distinct from ownedThrough, which is the date ownership ended.

candidates.label: datePublished
candidates.comment: A temporal release relation between a certification or creative work and its date of first publication or broadcast. Also called: publication date, broadcast date, release date. Examples: "Book" date published "1984-06-08", "TV Show Episode" date published "2023-01-01", "Certification" date published "2022-12-01". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the date of creation, and datePosted, which is for online listings.

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

chosen_property.label: madeChangesTo
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the entity or system that was modified by the subject.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly captures a software application making changes to a computer system.

candidates.label: legislationAmends
candidates.comment: A legislative modification relation between a piece of legislation and another legislation that it alters or revises. Also called amends law, modifies legislation, revises act, changes statute. Examples: Legislation A legislationAmends 'Legislation B'. The new act legislationAmends 'the previous statute'. This bill legislationAmends 'the tax code'. Distinct from legislationChanges, which is a broader term for any change, whereas legislationAmends specifically introduces legal changes.

candidates.label: legislationChanges
candidates.comment: A legislative alteration relation between a piece of legislation and another legislation that it modifies, replaces, corrects, or repeals. Also called alters law, modifies statute, replaces act, repeals legislation. Examples: Legislation X legislationChanges 'Legislation Y'. The new regulation legislationChanges 'several existing laws'. This amendment legislationChanges 'the previous version of the act'. Distinct from legislationAmends, which is a specific type of change (introducing legal changes), and legislationConsolidates, which is about creating a consolidated version.

candidates.label: releaseNotes
candidates.comment: A release notes relation between a software application and a description of changes in its current version. Also called changelog, version updates, new features. Examples: "A software application has release notes detailing 'bug fixes and performance improvements'.", "A mobile app update includes release notes about 'new UI design'.", "A game patch has release notes describing 'balance changes and new content'."

candidates.label: correction
candidates.comment: A modification relation between a creative work and the comment, text, or document detailing a correction to it. Also called: erratum, amendment, revision, fix. Examples: "News Article" correction "Editor's Note: A previous version of this article misstated...", "Software Manual" correction "See errata sheet for updates.", "Research Paper" correction "Correction published in Vol. 15, Issue 3.".

candidates.label: legislationCorrects
candidates.comment: A textual correction relation between two pieces of legislation, where one introduces non-legal changes to the other. Also called: corrects text, amends textually, revises without legal impact. Examples: "Act A legislationCorrects Act B", "Regulation X legislationCorrects Directive Y", "Law 123 legislationCorrects Statute 456". Distinct from legislationAmends, which introduces modifications with legal impact.

candidates.label: modifiedTime
candidates.comment: A modified time relation between a reservation and the date and time it was changed. Also called: last modified, update time, change timestamp. Examples: "Flight Reservation modifiedTime '2023-10-26T10:30:00Z'", "Hotel Booking modifiedTime '2023-11-01T15:00:00Z'", "Restaurant Reservation modifiedTime '2023-12-05T18:45:00Z'".

candidates.label: seasonalOverride
candidates.comment: A temporary modification of shipping conditions that applies during a specific limited period, often seasonal. Also called seasonal shipping change, temporary shipping rules, holiday shipping policy. Examples: `Standard Shipping Conditions` seasonalOverride `OpeningHoursSpecification for Christmas`, `Summer Shipping Policy` seasonalOverride `OpeningHoursSpecification for June-August`, `Black Friday Shipping` seasonalOverride `OpeningHoursSpecification for Nov 25-28`. Distinct from `returnPolicySeasonalOverride`, which is specific to return policies.

candidates.label: replacee
candidates.comment: A replacee relation between a replace action and the entity that is being substituted. Also called item replaced, old item. Examples: "A replace action involves a replacee 'old battery'.", "A document update replaces 'version 1.0'.", "A software upgrade replaces 'legacy system'.". Distinct from replacer, which is the entity doing the replacing.

candidates.label: returnPolicySeasonalOverride
candidates.comment: A temporary modification or override of a standard merchant return policy for a specific season or period. Also called seasonal return policy change, temporary return policy, holiday return policy. Examples: `Standard Return Policy` returnPolicySeasonalOverride `Holiday Return Policy 2023`, `Summer Sale Policy` returnPolicySeasonalOverride `Extended Return Window`, `Black Friday Policy` returnPolicySeasonalOverride `Special Return Terms`.

candidates.label: dateModified
candidates.comment: A temporal revision relation between a creative work or data feed item and the date it was most recently modified. Also called: last modified date, revision date, update date. Examples: "Wikipedia Article" date modified "2023-10-26T11:45:00Z", "Software Documentation" date modified "2023-09-01", "Data Feed Entry" date modified "2023-01-05". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the initial creation date.
